standard_prerequisites.name: Real integral Hodge conjecture and topological subgroup

statement.relation: Explicit BW1 prerequisite of the fixed PartII article; background only, no alias asserted to the published Inventiones version
statement.definition_summary: Let G=Gal(C/R). The restriction of alpha in H_G^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)) to X(R), followed by the canonical map(1.57), has components alpha_p for p congruent to k modulo2. The topological subgroup0 is defined by alpha_{k+i}=Sq^i(alpha_k) for even i, with negative squares zero. For1-cycles on a D-dimensional variety, k=D-1 and Remark1.20(i) equivalently requires alpha_p=0 for p<k. Over real numbers, Hdg_G0 intersects this subgroup with the inverse image of ordinary Hodge(k,k) classes. RIHC means surjectivity of CH^k(X) to Hdg_G0. PartII keeps its stated scope R=real numbers or H^2(O_X)=0.

Keep the real cubic odd-degree/norm branch together with its previously supplied conic theorem
Do not add degree4 over an anisotropic conic as an unconditional fifth case
proof_roadmap: Construct algebraic representatives for classes supported on singular real fibers using SNC resolution, Ext torsion-freeness and mixed-Hodge vanishing.
Build the quotient-semi-algebraic Leray spectral sequence and prove injectivity of restriction to fibers over a suitable affine base.
Remove multisections or sections to reduce a class to degree zero, distinguishing even and odd degrees and the exact real-fiber hypotheses.
Use fiber detection and localization to recover global algebraicity.
For the unrestricted real cubic case, pass to an odd-degree extension with a line, reuse the conic-bundle theorem and combine odd annihilation with the2-norm.
items.difficulty_reason: H3: the theorem combines a real singular-fiber cycle construction through Ext groups and mixed-Hodge vanishing with a quotient-semi-algebraic Leray spectral sequence, integral fiber detection and arithmetic section/multisection arguments. The real cubic branch additionally uses an odd Galois orbit and coprime norm descent through the conic theorem. Easy degrees5/7/9 and short corollaries do not create extra advanced IDs; the whole nonroutine author core is supplied as one parent.
